title: India declare at 720 for nine in Wellington, their highest Test total outside Asia
dek: Rishabh Pant's 128 and Dhruv Jurel's 78 took India to the biggest total ever made in a Test in New Zealand and a lead of 352 on the fourth day.
author: Declaration Desk
body:
India declared their first innings at 720 for nine on the fourth day of the first Test against New Zealand at the Basin Reserve in Wellington on Sunday, the highest total ever made in a Test in New Zealand, leaving the hosts 352 behind with a day and a session to play.

Rishabh Pant made 128, his ninth Test century, and Dhruv Jurel 78 off 79 balls as India added 234 runs in two sessions from their overnight 486 for four. Captain Shubman Gill declared at about 7.13 am IST, when Jurel was stumped off Glenn Phillips, according to reports. New Zealand began their second innings needing to bat for well over a day to save the match.

## The day's play

India resumed with Pant on 55 and the nightwatchman Anshul Kamboj yet to score. Kamboj made 38 off 42 balls in a fifth-wicket stand of more than 50 before he was caught off Phillips, according to reports. Pant reached three figures with a six off Phillips shortly after 5 am IST and was out for 128 off 153 balls, with 10 fours and six sixes, caught off Rachin Ravindra just before lunch, which India took at 629 for six.

After the break Jurel reached his fifty and India kept attacking. Akash Deep hit 13 off five balls before he fell, and Jurel's dismissal brought the declaration. Phillips, an occasional off-spinner, took three wickets. The fast bowler Jacob Duffy finished with one for 201 from 33 overs, the second-most expensive figures by a New Zealand bowler in a Test innings, according to reports.

Six Indian batters passed fifty: KL Rahul (136), Pant (128), Gill (98), Yashasvi Jaiswal (85), Devdutt Padikkal (80) and Jurel (78).

## The records

India's total beats the West Indies' 660 for five declared at the same ground in 1995 as the highest by a visiting team in New Zealand, and New Zealand's own 715 for six declared against Bangladesh at Hamilton in 2019 as the highest in any Test in the country, according to reports.

It is India's third-highest Test total, behind 759 for seven declared against England in Chennai in 2016 and 726 for nine declared against Sri Lanka at the Brabourne Stadium in Mumbai in 2009, and their highest outside Asia, ahead of 705 for seven declared at Sydney in 2004, according to reports.

## What happens next

New Zealand were bowled out for 368 in their first innings, built around Henry Nicholls's unbeaten 175, with Jasprit Bumrah taking four wickets. They need 352 to make India bat again. The final day is Monday, 23 November, with play due to start at 3.30 am IST. A win would give India an early lead in the series and valuable points in the World Test Championship.

This report will be updated at the end of the day's play.
